verdict.rationale: Visa documents a self-serve merchant-side onboarding path: an Intelligent Commerce sandbox sign-up form with terms acceptance that lets you send test transactions. Separately, the open Trusted Agent Protocol spec and reference implementation (cdn-proxy, merchant-backend) let a merchant verify agent signatures against Visa's public JWKS without coordinating with Visa. However, production access is gated ('Contact Visa for fees in Production'), and the product is still 'in the process of development and deployment'. Missing for 10: a self-serve production enablement path (setting or agreement), a documented step-by-step merchant go-live flow for accepting agent traffic, and independent hands-on corroboration of merchant onboarding.

support.subject: As a merchant, I have a documented self-serve path to start accepting agent traffic — enable a setting, sign an agreement, or publish an endpoint

citations.quote: After completing the evaluation registration process, you will be able to send test transactions
Free to use in Sandbox. Contact Visa for fees in Production.
merchants verify against Visa's public keys at https://mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks
The repo ships a complete sample ecosystem — tap-agent, merchant-frontend, cdn-proxy (RFC 9421 verification), merchant-backend, and agent-registry
